title: Buffon's Noodle: Additivity of Expected Crossings over Concatenation
description: Establishes the missing structural lemma of the Buffon family: the concrete expected-crossing functional E(γ, a, b, d) = (1/(πd)) ∫_a^b ∫_0^π |γ'ₓ sinθ + γ'_y cosθ| dθ dt is additive over concatenation of the parameter interval. A noodle traversed from a to b and split at an interior point c has expected crossings equal to the sum over its two halves; iterating gives additivity over an arbitrary n-piece partition (the formal 'a noodle is a sum of needles' decomposition). Self-contained (Mathlib-only): the parent's functional is reproduced by definition. 0 axioms, 0 sorries; host-verified against Mathlib 4.26.0 (lake env lean).

mathlibDependencies.description: ∫_a^b f + ∫_b^c f = ∫_a^c f for interval-integrable f
Σ_{k ∈ Ico m n} ∫_{a k}^{a (k+1)} f = ∫_{a m}^{a n} f for a chain of points
A continuous function is interval-integrable on any [a, b]
c * Σ f = Σ (c * f), used to push the 1/(πd) factor through the sum

overview.historicalContext: Joseph-Émile Barbier's 1860 extension of Buffon's needle problem states that a planar curve of arc length $L$ — a 'noodle' of any shape — has expected crossing count $E = 2L/(\pi d)$ when dropped on a floor ruled with lines spaced $d$ apart. The standard heuristic argument runs: approximate the noodle by a polygonal chain of short needles; the expected number of crossings is *additive*, so it equals the sum of the per-segment expectations; each short needle contributes proportionally to its length; therefore the total is proportional to total length, independent of shape. The additivity step — that expected crossings of a concatenated curve equal the sum over the pieces — is the structural backbone of this argument, yet it is the one part the parent formalization chain never recorded as a standalone lemma.
overview.problemStatement: The parent file `BuffonsNeedleOQ01OQ01OQ01` proves the *value* of the concrete expected-crossing functional $E(\gamma, a, b, d) = \frac{1}{\pi d}\int_a^b\!\int_0^\pi |\gamma'_x(t)\sin\theta + \gamma'_y(t)\cos\theta|\,d\theta\,dt$. This entry asks: is $E$ additive over concatenation of the parameter interval, $E(\gamma, a, b, d) = E(\gamma, a, c, d) + E(\gamma, c, b, d)$, and does it iterate to an arbitrary partition? This is the formal 'noodle = sum of needles' decomposition underlying Barbier's argument.
overview.proofStrategy: Reproduce the parent's functional definitions (`angularIntegrand`, `expectedCrossings`) verbatim so the file depends only on Mathlib, then observe that additivity lives entirely in the *outer* interval integral $\int_a^b$. The inner angular integral and the constant factor $1/(\pi d)$ are inert. One split point follows from `intervalIntegral.integral_add_adjacent_intervals` after factoring out $1/(\pi d)$ with `mul_add`; the integrability side conditions are discharged from continuity of the angular integrand via `Continuous.intervalIntegrable`. Two split points compose two single splits with `IntervalIntegrable.trans` and `ring`. The general n-piece partition uses `intervalIntegral.sum_integral_adjacent_intervals_Ico` followed by `Finset.mul_sum`.
keyInsights: Additivity of the Buffon functional is a property of the *outer* integral only. The angular integrand and the geometric normalization $1/(\pi d)$ pass through untouched, so the whole content reduces to additivity of $\int_a^b$ over adjacent intervals — a Mathlib lemma. The honest framing: this is the family's missing structural lemma, not a deep theorem.

Stating the integrability hypotheses precisely is the real work. `integral_add_adjacent_intervals` requires `IntervalIntegrable` on each piece; the entry provides both the raw form (hypotheses explicit) and a `_of_continuous` form that discharges them from `Continuous (angularIntegrand γ)`, the natural condition for C¹ curves.

The general partition lemma exposes a subtle Mathlib API seam: `sum_integral_adjacent_intervals_Ico` quantifies its integrability hypothesis over membership in `Set.Ico m n`, while its conclusion sums over `Finset.Ico m n`. The entry keeps the public hypothesis in terms of `Finset.Ico` (matching the sum) and converts at the application site via `Finset.mem_Ico.mpr (Set.mem_Ico.mp ·)` — a one-line bridge that an earlier hand-verification missed and machine-checking caught.

Making the file self-contained (Mathlib-only) rather than importing the parent is a deliberate verification choice: the concrete functional is reproduced by definition, so external checkers need only Mathlib, not the project's internal proof chain.

The split point `c` need not lie between `a` and `b`. Because Mathlib's oriented interval integrals satisfy `∫_a^b = -∫_b^a` by convention, `expectedCrossings_additive` holds for *any* real `c`, not just an interior point of a genuine sub-interval — the orientation bookkeeping that a hand proof would need to case-split on is handled for free by the integral's sign convention.

sections.title: Module Header and Definitions
sections.summary: Imports Mathlib; module docstring documenting the lineage from BuffonsNeedleOQ01OQ01OQ01. Defines `angularIntegrand` (the inner ∫_0^π angular integral at a parameter t) and `expectedCrossings` (the full functional (1/(πd)) ∫_a^b angularIntegrand), reproduced verbatim from the parent so the file is Mathlib-only.

sections.title: Degenerate Interval
sections.summary: `expectedCrossings_self`: an empty parameter interval [a, a] contributes 0 crossings, via `integral_same` and `mul_zero`. Tagged `@[simp]`.

sections.title: Additivity Across One Split Point
sections.summary: `expectedCrossings_additive`: for any interior c, E(γ,a,b,d) = E(γ,a,c,d) + E(γ,c,b,d), given interval-integrability on each piece (no ordering of a,c,b required). Proof factors out 1/(πd) with `mul_add`, then applies `integral_add_adjacent_intervals`. `expectedCrossings_additive_of_continuous` discharges the integrability hypotheses from `Continuous (angularIntegrand γ)`.

sections.title: Additivity Across Two Split Points
sections.summary: `expectedCrossings_additive3`: a three-piece noodle. Composes two single-split applications, combining the right two pieces' integrability with `IntervalIntegrable.trans`, then `ring`.

sections.title: General Partition Additivity (Noodle = Σ Needles)
sections.summary: `expectedCrossings_partition`: for a chain of parameter points pts m ≤ … ≤ pts n, E over [pts m, pts n] equals the sum of E over the n−m consecutive pieces. Uses `sum_integral_adjacent_intervals_Ico` (with a Finset.Ico → Set.Ico membership bridge) and `Finset.mul_sum`.

conclusion.summary: Proves the Buffon family's missing structural lemma: the concrete expected-crossing functional is additive over concatenation of the parameter interval, from a single split point up to an arbitrary n-piece partition. Combined with the parent's shape-independence result it gives the 'noodle = Σ needles' decomposition that underlies Barbier's heuristic. 0 axioms, 0 sorries; host-verified against Mathlib 4.26.0.
conclusion.implications: Additivity is the algebraic skeleton of Barbier's theorem: once expected crossings are additive over pieces and proportional to length on each short needle, shape-independence of the constant 2/(πd) follows. Stating it for the exact functional the family uses, with explicit integrability hypotheses, makes the partition step of the Barbier argument fully machine-checkable rather than heuristic.
openQuestions: Can the partition additivity proved here be combined with the parent's per-needle value to formalize the full Buffon–Barbier theorem $E = 2L/(\pi d)$ for an arbitrary C¹ noodle — i.e. take the limit of the polygonal-chain approximation and show it converges to the arc-length functional?

The functional is defined for C¹ curves via the velocity $\gamma'$. Does additivity extend to merely rectifiable curves parametrized by arc length, where $\gamma'$ exists only almost everywhere, so that the 'noodle = Σ needles' decomposition covers the full generality of Barbier's original statement?

Does the same additive-over-partition structure carry to the higher-dimensional Cauchy–Crofton setting (expected intersections of a surface with a family of planes in $\mathbb{R}^3$), or does the orientation bookkeeping that oriented interval integrals handle for free in 1D require genuinely new machinery there?

crossReferences.description: Establishes the value of the concrete expected-crossing functional (Buffon–Barbier formula for C¹ curves); this entry supplies the additivity/partition structure of that same functional.
Origin of the concrete double-integral definition `concreteSmoothExpectedCrossings` reproduced here as `expectedCrossings`.
The original Buffon's Needle formalization at the root of this open-question lineage.

references.text: Barbier, J.-É. (1860). Note sur le problème de l'aiguille et le jeu du joint couvert. J. Math. Pures Appl. The additivity-and-proportionality argument formalized here is the backbone of Barbier's extension.
Santaló, L. A. (1976). Integral Geometry and Geometric Probability. Addison-Wesley. Treats expected crossing counts and the Cauchy–Crofton formula.

theorems.name: expectedCrossings_self
theorems.description: An empty parameter interval contributes no crossings.

theorems.name: expectedCrossings_additive
theorems.statement: IntervalIntegrable (angularIntegrand γ) volume a c → IntervalIntegrable (angularIntegrand γ) volume c b → expectedCrossings γ a b d = expectedCrossings γ a c d + expectedCrossings γ c b d
theorems.description: Additivity across one interior split point.

theorems.name: expectedCrossings_additive_of_continuous
theorems.statement: Continuous (angularIntegrand γ) → expectedCrossings γ a b d = expectedCrossings γ a c d + expectedCrossings γ c b d
theorems.description: Single-split additivity with integrability discharged from continuity.

theorems.name: expectedCrossings_additive3
theorems.statement: expectedCrossings γ a b d = expectedCrossings γ a c₁ d + expectedCrossings γ c₁ c₂ d + expectedCrossings γ c₂ b d (given integrability on each of the three pieces)
theorems.description: Additivity across two split points (three-piece noodle).

theorems.name: expectedCrossings_partition
theorems.statement: m ≤ n → (∀ k ∈ Finset.Ico m n, IntervalIntegrable (angularIntegrand γ) volume (pts k) (pts (k+1))) → expectedCrossings γ (pts m) (pts n) d = ∑ k ∈ Finset.Ico m n, expectedCrossings γ (pts k) (pts (k+1)) d
theorems.description: Additivity over an arbitrary n-piece partition: the 'noodle = Σ needles' decomposition.
